1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable font sizes and line spacing, though letter spacing is ordinary rather than notably generous.

2.why: Headings, labels, and instructions contain no italics or all-caps and appear only as short one-to-three-sentence blocks.

3.why: All content sits in a narrow single-column card with full-width inputs and large buttons that would reflow well on a phone, although the supplied screenshots are desktop-width.

4.why: Every instruction observed (e.g., 'Enter the six-digit identity code', 'Each recovery code works once...') is one to three short sentences in plain language.

5.why: Most fields carry placeholder examples ('marcus@example.com', '6 digits', 'ABCD-1234-EF56-7890'), but the identity-code field and the settings authenticator-code field show no example.

6.why: No long instructional block gates progress; the only dense text block is the simulation's Logs panel, which steps 2 and 12 do direct the user to read for test codes.

7.why: The secret and the ten recovery codes are shown as plain text with no copy, download, or print control, and step 4 even requires re-typing the secret into a 'Manual secret entry' field.

8.why: No QR code or scannable alternative is displayed on the provisioning screen — only the text secret — despite the copy referencing 'scanning a code'.

9.why: The screenshots show only standard text inputs with no visible autocomplete attributes or password-manager affordances, so support can neither be confirmed nor denied.

10.why: Each screen has a bold heading naming the step and one dominant blue primary button, though no progress indicator shows the user's position in the overall flow.

11.why: Enrolment steps mostly ask one thing, but step 4 requests two inputs at once and the MFA settings screen presents four simultaneous actions (Test, Use recovery code, Regenerate, Log out).

12.why: Success messages do state outcomes ('Authenticator verification succeeded.', 'Recovery code accepted and permanently consumed.', 'Challenge ready...'), but most omit what comes next and the error state gives no guidance.

13.why: A 'Start over' link, penalty-free retries, and code regeneration exist, but recovery codes 'will not be shown again' and there is no reveal/hide control.

14.why: The only error observed — 'The request could not be completed.' — neither identifies the problem nor explains how to fix it, though it does not blame the user.

15.why: No countdowns, session-timeout warnings, or code-entry time limits appear on any screen.
